deck: The share rises when the comparison uses filings listing only AI issues.

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: Lobbyists named for network clients gave personally to committees linked to 304 serving members.
deck: The first bar counts lobbyists whose firm was registered for a network client when they gave. The second also requires the client’s filings to name the lobbyist.
note: The givers used their own money. These third-party gifts can count toward a seat in the opening chamber. The filings leave any effect on a vote open.
bridge: Career records connect congressional offices and the network in another way. Where did people go?
source: Lobbyist contribution reports and federal registrations · Gift dates Feb. 22, 2021–June 30, 2026

act: Deeper · III · How the lobbying works
head: More people moved from Capitol Hill to the network and its firms than the other way in these records.
deck: Horizon Institute runs a fellowship whose hosts include members’ offices and committees. Its placements account for the moves into Congress shown here.
note: Horizon pays the stipend and the host directs the work. The records establish the roles people held. Back in the main story, why do Lieu and Tillis get one seat each?
source: Congressional payroll, lobbying disclosures, staffing records and Horizon’s placement roster
